title: ExceptionalSiteRealization
statement: For a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $W$, and the actual etale/pro-etale system comparison in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], use the quotient scalar coordinates of [def-pur-adic-proetale-realization] and [def-pur-adic-etale-realization]. Define the ordinary direct-image comparison uniquely by equality with the recorded underlying set-sheaf map on every section. Define the inverse-image comparison as its unique adjunction mate, with the full Hom-transpose equation for every pair of modules and every morphism.

proof.text: Recover the underlying direct comparison as the transpose of the level counit using levelTranspose at the counit and the adjunction identity. Naturality of the set-valued unit then expresses this formula on every generalized section.

Use the product of the underlying module sheaf with itself as test sheaf. Apply the algebraic inverse image moduleAdd graph equation to the two projections and addition. The counit is additive, so the underlying right comparison preserves addition.

The constant singleton presheaf is already a sheaf, so its sheafification unit is an isomorphism. The sheafification adjunction therefore evaluates coefficientConstantSection at every singleton section as the actual constant coefficient unit. Apply moduleSMul to singleton times the underlying module sheaf. The constants equation for the ordinary comparison and counit linearity show that the right comparison preserves constant scalar multiplication.

The constantCommuteCompose sheafification equation identifies the constant ring units after forgetting commutativity. Consequently the same section maps are linear in the explicit quotient coordinates on both sites. Bundle these maps into a natural transformation of module-valued sheaves. The underlying set comparison is invertible on every section, hence so are these linear maps and the resulting natural transformation. Sectionwise extensionality proves its uniqueness.

Take the inverse mate of the direct comparison along the two ordinary site adjunctions. Both vertical realization functors are equivalences, so the inverse mate is invertible. Its inverse is the required inverse-image comparison.

The inverse-mate unit equation, functoriality and naturality of the right comparison give the full Hom-transpose formula for every morphism. For uniqueness specialize the formula to the identity at each inverse-image object and use injectivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence. Extensionality then identifies the inverse natural transformations and their isomorphisms.
